questions.prompt: A classmate says, If your charisma collapses under pressure, you probably never had real charisma to begin with. What correction fits this chapter best?
choices: That may be true because pressure mostly reveals fixed social limits
The chapter argues that pressure can distort signals through obstacles without proving permanent lack
The chapter says charisma matters only in calm rooms, so pressure is not a fair test

explanation.gentle: The chapter treats a bad room as distortion before destiny. Pressure can interfere with presence, power, and warmth without proving they were never there.
explanation.direct: The chapter's whole point is obstacle language over trait verdicts. Pressure can twist the social read before it says anything final about identity.
explanation.competitive: That claim sounds tough-minded, but it is too blunt. The chapter is built to stop that lazy leap from collapse to destiny.

questions.prompt: What is usually happening first when presence fails in this chapter's model?
choices: Attention is splitting inward toward anxiety, distraction, or self-monitoring
The person is becoming kinder than the room knows how to handle
Status is rising so quickly that warmth can no longer register

explanation.gentle: Presence weakens when the room can no longer feel full attention. The wrong answers drift into warmth or status rather than divided attention.
explanation.direct: Presence fails through inward collapse, not through excess kindness or rising status. The chapter keeps tying this problem to split attention.
explanation.competitive: The room feels absence before it starts theorizing about your rank. Presence dies when your focus leaves the interaction.

questions.prompt: Power and warmth are most clearly separated in which contrast?
choices: Power is eye contact, while warmth is smiling more often
Power is speaking first, while warmth is speaking last
Power is visible consequence, while warmth is visible goodwill

explanation.gentle: The chapter keeps these signals distinct by tying power to consequence and warmth to trust. The other answers reduce them to shallow behaviors.
explanation.direct: Power and warmth solve different problems. One tells the room your words matter, and the other tells the room your force is safe enough to trust.
explanation.competitive: This chapter hates decorative definitions. Consequence and goodwill are the real split, not eye-contact tricks.

questions.prompt: Iris notices before a client call that she is listening to her own fear more than to the room. Which diagnosis fits the chapter?
choices: Her main obstacle is split attention, so presence is the first signal under attack
Her main obstacle is excess warmth, so power should be ignored for now
Her main obstacle is low intelligence, which the chapter says no signal can cover up

explanation.gentle: Iris is not failing because she lacks ability. She is losing presence because anxiety is trapping attention inward before the interaction begins.
explanation.direct: The chapter would name this as attention failure first. Presence is weakening because self-monitoring is displacing real contact with the room.
explanation.competitive: Iris is leaving the room before the client arrives. That is presence failure, not fate.

questions.prompt: Karim softens a necessary feedback point three times and apologizes before the core sentence lands. What is the chapter most likely to say?
choices: He is increasing warmth in the best possible way
He is draining power by retreating from the consequence of his own message
He is proving that presence matters more than power in all feedback situations

explanation.gentle: Karim may still mean well, but the room feels less weight behind the message. That is why the chapter treats this as power loss rather than kindness alone.
explanation.direct: The issue is visible retreat. When Karim apologizes before the point lands, consequence drains out of the message and power weakens.
explanation.competitive: That is not tact. It is shrinkage dressed up as care, and the room feels the drop in weight.

questions.prompt: Tessa enters a personal conversation already planning protective lines and feeling less curious. Which signal is most likely to distort first?
choices: Power, because any personal conversation always becomes a status contest
Warmth, because self-protection is becoming more visible than goodwill
Presence, because warmth and power never matter in personal life

explanation.gentle: Tessa still may care about the other person, but the brace is arriving first. The chapter would call that a warmth problem rooted in self-protection.
explanation.direct: Self-conscious defensiveness cools warmth before the conversation even starts. The issue is not that caring disappeared, but that the room will not feel it clearly.
explanation.competitive: Armor beats intention if it gets there first. That is exactly why warmth is the signal at risk.

questions.prompt: In a graduate seminar, Nolan starts monitoring how he sounds and stops really hearing the room. What does this example add beyond simple nerves language?
choices: It shows that pressure matters only in school contexts
It shows that smart people are usually less charismatic than confident people
It shows that the first distortion can be identified as presence failure rather than left as a vague feeling

explanation.gentle: Nolan's example becomes more useful because it names the signal being distorted. The chapter wants that specificity instead of a foggy nerves label.
explanation.direct: The chapter is training diagnostic precision. Nolan is not just nervous; he is losing presence through inward monitoring.
explanation.competitive: Vague nerves talk would hide the miss. Naming presence failure turns the room into data.

questions.prompt: Miles feels split attention, then shrinking power, then defensive coldness before a social gathering even starts. Why does that sequence matter?
choices: Because stacked obstacles are easier to understand once you identify the first failure point
Because the chapter says later distortions matter more than the first one
Because any sequence with three steps proves charisma is mostly chemistry

explanation.gentle: The sequence matters because one obstacle can trigger the next. The chapter wants the reader to find where the chain started.
explanation.direct: Stacking changes diagnosis. If you know the first failure point, the rest of the collapse becomes easier to interpret and later repair.
explanation.competitive: Find the first crack and the rest stops feeling magical. Miss it and the whole spiral keeps masquerading as personality.

questions.prompt: Why does this chapter insist on obstacle diagnosis before offering repair?
choices: Because repair is impossible unless the person becomes completely calm first
Because one generic fix would miss the difference between split attention, shrinking power, and defensive warmth loss
Because diagnosis is more important than social results in every context

explanation.gentle: Repair has to fit the distortion. The chapter first separates the obstacles so the next chapter does not treat every weak room as the same problem.
explanation.direct: Diagnosis comes first because the failures differ. A presence problem, a power problem, and a warmth problem should not be repaired as though they were identical.
explanation.competitive: If you cannot name the miss, your fix becomes theater. The chapter would rather make the failure readable first.

questions.prompt: Chapter 4 is titled Overcoming the Obstacles. What is the most natural bridge from this chapter into that one?
choices: Once the triad fails under pressure, the reader should ignore the room until perfect calm returns
Once obstacles exist, the later chapters become mostly optional because the core lesson is complete
Once the first distortion is visible, the next question is how to interrupt it before the room hardens around it

explanation.gentle: This chapter makes failure points legible. The next chapter naturally asks how to interrupt them in time.
explanation.direct: The bridge is practical: diagnosis sets up repair. Once the first distortion can be seen, the next useful move is learning how to stop it from owning the room.
explanation.competitive: Legibility is not the finish. It is the setup for attack, and Chapter 4 is where that attack begins.
